practice_span: I have been at the loom since I was fourteen. It has been thirty-six years.
local_belonging_phrase: “Chanderi cloth is woven in the lanes of Chanderi. The sound of a loom comes from every third house here.”
ecological_input: Thread breaks less in the damp of the rains, so we set the fine warp in that season. In summer, keeping the loom in a pit stays cool.
place_change: Electricity came, and powerlooms with it. The old pit looms became fewer, and shops and tourists around the fort increased.
emotion_about_place_change: “It is good that tourists come. But they buy from the shop and leave, and nobody comes to see the loom.”
teacher_name_relation: My father, Abdul Karim Ansari. I learned the buti work from my aunt.
teaching_memory: One day my father held my woven length up to the sunlight from the window and said, “See, where does the light catch?” A thin line showed. He said nothing more, and just put the cloth back.
remembered_phrase_gesture: “Thread doesn't shout, it just breaks.” He would say this while passing his palm over the warp.
family_generations: My grandfather and father were weavers. My brother and I weave. My daughter Sana makes designs, and my son is studying in Bhopal.
transmission_strength: Plain weaving and nalphera are learned at home. Children see them every day.
transmission_weakness: The old ashrafi buti and the fine borders. Complete samples of these remain with only two or three elders now.
teaching_difficulty: Learning takes two or three years and wages are low. Boys see a city job as more dependable.
primary_material: Silk warp, fine cotton weft, and zari for the butis.
material_origin: Silk comes from Bengaluru, yarn from Coimbatore and zari from Surat. It reaches us through the master weaver.
first_contact: As a child I sat filling bobbins. I still remember the smoothness of silk on my fingers and the smell of the starch.
material_special: The warp is very fine and the starch light. That gives the cloth the transparency and sheen Chanderi is known for.
material_in_hands: A good warp hums slightly under the hand. If the thread stays straight without stretching, the weaving will go well.
material_feels_wrong: When fuzz rises on the thread, or the warp feels slack on one side, or the sound of the loom changes.
correction_action: I stop weaving. I apply a little starch to the warp and tighten the slack threads one at a time. Hurrying ruins the whole length.
material_change_gain: Good silk thread is easier to get now. The colours are also faster, and customers complain less.
material_change_loss: Real zari became expensive, so imitation zari is used now. Local yarn doesn't have the same softness either.
occasion_of_use: Weddings, Eid, Teej. In cities the sari is also worn to offices and functions.
sensory_scene: A wedding evening, the scent of loban, the sound of the dholak, and old women touching and counting the butis on the pallu.
remembered_community_phrase: “A Chanderi sari wears the breeze.” That is what my mother used to say.
special_vs_everyday: Plain cloth and small butis for every day. A bride's sari has handmade zari butis and takes a month and a half.
special_object_rule: We set the warp of a bride's outfit after Friday prayers. No other work is done on that loom that day.
not_for_sale_example: My father's old hand-drawn buti designs. I don't give these to any company.
why_protected: They are the capital of this house. Once a design goes out, next month it appears on a powerloom.
safer_alternative: Sana's new designs and plain lengths. I can show pictures of those and video of the weaving.
pride_moment: At an artisans' fair in Delhi an old woman showed me her wedding sari. My grandfather had woven it. I recognised the border.
recognition_by_others: That woman, and the master craftsmen in our neighbourhood, who now come to me to set their warp.
loss_if_stopped: The hand that weaves fine warp would be gone. The name Chanderi would remain, but the cloth would be a machine's.
key_stakeholder_of_loss: The families in this neighbourhood who live by the loom, especially the women who do bobbin and buti work.
change_in_lifetime: Before, master weavers decided everything. Now some weavers sell online themselves, though very few.
artisan_initiated_change: I sent my daughter to learn design alongside the loom. Now we make our own samples, and take direct orders with three families.
desired_keep: The handloom, the hand-made buti, and the way of working together in the neighbourhood.
desired_let_go: Complete dependence on master weavers, and the idea that daughters will only fill bobbins.
strength_anchor: My hand is clean at setting the warp. I can set the finest thread without breaking it, and catch a loom fault by its sound.
concern_anchor: Powerloom cloth is being sold as Chanderi. Who will explain the difference between real and fake to the customer?
shareable_content: The method of weaving, the loom, my name, Sana's new designs.
private_content: My father's designs, our wage accounts and dealings with the master weaver.
desired_change: Direct orders from shops, with the weaver's name written on every sari.
desired_continuity: A Chanderi sari will be woven on a handloom only, whatever the price.
learning_story: Once in a hurry I set a dry warp before the rains. On the third day a hundred threads broke, and the whole week was lost. Since then I decide by touching the warp, not by looking at the calendar.
emotional_story: After my father died his loom stayed shut for two months. The day I first ran it, my mother came out of the kitchen at the sound. She said nothing, she just stood there.
clarification_story: A buyer said, it is so thin, it must be weak. I showed them a fifty-year-old sari that is still worn. Fine does not mean weak.
outsider_misunderstanding: People think Chanderi is just a design. Really, it is the fineness of the warp and the work of the hand.
